To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

creatine plus caffeine supplementation does not affect the lean body mass of either sedentated or exercised rats, while caffeine supplementation reduces the percentage of body fat in both sedentated and exercised animals, and that vertical jumping training increases the lean body mass (water and protein) and reduces the fat mass in rats.
High combined doses of caffeine and creatine do not affect the LMB composition of sedentary or exercise rats, however, supplementation with caffeine alone reduces the fat percentage.
high doses of creatinine and caffeine, either alone or combined, do not influence lean body mass (water, protein and fat) composition of rats submitted for vertical jumping training.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of creatine and/or caffeine supplementation on LBM composition of animals submitted to a vertical jump training program.

the effects of creatine supplementation on LBM composition of exercised and sedentary rats, and the effects of a high dose of caffeine supplementation on LBM in rats submitted to vertical jump training, either solely or in combination with creatine.
the effects of creatine and/or caffeine supplementation, either alone or combined, on the lean body weight composition of exercised animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
creatine and caffeine alone or together do not affect the LMB composition in sedentary rats.
creatine supplementation alone or combined with caffeine did not affect the LMB composition of rats.
caffeine supplementation, either alone or associated with creatine supplementation, does not affect the lean body mass in rats submitted to vertical jump training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

caffeine supplementation reduces the body fat percentage and increases the percentage of protein in the carcass, and vertical jumping training reduces the fat percentage, increases the percentage of water and protein in the carcasses of the rats.
caffeine supplementation reduces the body fat content in rats submitted to vertical jump training.

creatine and caffeine combined does not affect the body composition of rats submitted or not to vertical jumping training, while caffeine supplementation alone reduces fat percentage in sedentary rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
caffeine supplementation alone reduces fat mass, while creatine supplementation alone has no effect.
creatine supplementation is ineffective for fat loss and caffeine supplementation may be effective for this purpose.
creatine supplementation does not affect LBM composition, while caffeine supplementation alone reduces fat percentage in rats.
